operator.dispatch: Resume could remember scroll position within a note

context_of_record: lands on top of the PR #628 three-page toolbar (trace 1a19acb6ec437e25 'the same three-page treatment could get search/resume on exam-questions and flashcards'), which itself stood on the three-trace arc 1a1954cacb3d2ab5 (MathsGenie search/Resume/tick on the revision-notes select page) + 1a195fd0b0947695 (scroll law of record: a note becomes read only when its END footnote strip scrolls into view, never on page entry; notes-only ring scope) + 1a1982281a3d7a65 (each select page owns its own ring denominator). What Resume did NOT remember was WHERE in the note the learner stopped — every resume landed at the top. This run executes the new order: resume restores the saved reading position.

what_lands.law_store: apps/hub/src/lib/note-scroll.ts (new) — per-course localStorage scroll memory syllabai-hub:note-scroll:<course> as {[noteId]: {frac, at}}, bounded MAX_ENTRIES=120 (oldest-at evicted, freshly written note always survives its own write); FRACTION not pixels (bodies reflow across visits — fonts/KaTeX/images/corpus updates — a fraction degrades gracefully, a pixel offset rots); SEPARATE namespace from the learner progress overlay so high-frequency position writes never churn the object the rings read, and because notesRead entries only exist once a note is READ (scrolled to its end) while resume must be able to point at a note the learner is mid-way through; laws owned here so island, index and tests share one truth: SAVE GATE (sub-2% positions refused — not reading positions, they cannot manufacture resume targets), RESUME BAND [2%,98%] (interrupted reads restore exactly; a position at/after 98% means the note was read to its end — the read event fires exactly there — so that note opens fresh from the top: 'resuming' a finished note at its footer strip carries no information), pickResumeNoteId joins notesRead.at ∪ noteScrolls.at → most recently ENGAGED note (engagement-based posture matching the exam-questions resume 'most recently scored part' and the flashcards resume 'most recently rated card'; a mid-note scroll outranks a finished read it never returned to; stale note ids outside the course's corpus never win)
what_lands.island: apps/hub/src/app/courses/[course]/revision-notes/[noteId]/note-scroll-memory.tsx (new, renders nothing) — SAVE leg: window-scroll fraction into the store, throttled to one write per 400ms, flushed on pagehide / visibilitychange-hidden / unmount so the throttle can never eat the learner's final position; sub-0.2% movements ignored (no churn); RESTORE leg: consumes the ?resume=1 intent stamped by the notes index Resume href (consumed immediately via history.replaceState so refreshes and shared URLs stay honest), restores the saved fraction only inside the resume band, re-asserts the target at 0/120/350/700/1200ms against the note's asynchronous height settle (KaTeX, images), cancels instantly on learner input (wheel/touchstart/keydown) — the island never fights the person reading; instant scrollTo (never smooth) so prefers-reduced-motion is respected by default
what_lands.index: notes-index.tsx — resume target widens from reads-only (max notesRead.at) to max engagement across notesRead ∪ noteScrolls (pickResumeNoteId over the course's known note ids); Resume href stamps ?resume=1; the toolbar comment block restates the law. Consequence disclosed: the Resume button can now first-appear for a learner whose only engagement is a mid-note scroll (previously required ≥1 completed read) — that is the point of the order ('continue where you left off'), and it aligns notes resume with the other two select pages' engagement-based posture
what_lands.note_reader: page.tsx mounts NoteScrollMemory next to NoteFootnote (server component mounting a client island, the NoteFootnote pattern)
